# Using the Bioconductor Zulip chat {.unnumbered}

Bioconductor uses [Zulip](https://zulip.com/), a freely accessible, open-source chat platform, for community discussion, brainstorming, coordination, introductions, announcements, mentoring, working groups, and event planning.

New users can sign up at <https://chat.bioconductor.org/>. See [Using the Bioconductor Zulip chat](using_the_zulip_chat.qmd) for an introduction to channels, topics, and getting started.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Are you in the right place?

For an overview of all community communication channels, see [Community communication channels](community_communication_channels.qmd).
:::

## Understanding channels and topics

Zulip organises messages into **channels** and **topics**:

- A **channel** is a broad area of interest, such as `education-and-training` or `events`.
- A **topic** is the subject of a conversation within that channel. Think of it like an **email subject line**.

For example, a conversation in `education-and-training` might have the topic "Finding introductory RNA-seq materials".

## Starting or joining a conversation

**To ask a new question or start a conversation**, choose a relevant channel and give your topic a short, descriptive title, just as you would write a subject line for a new email.

**To reply to a conversation you are reading**, write in that conversation's existing topic, just as you would reply to an email thread.

You don't need to search through old topics or find a perfect match before asking a new question. If someone knows of a related discussion, they can point you to it.

::: {.callout-tip title="Not sure where to post?"}
Try `#general`, or `#no-stupid-questions` for questions about Bioconductor, R, and the community.

You don't need to find the perfect channel or topic title before posting. Other community members can help, and messages can be moved if needed.

For help troubleshooting a specific Bioconductor package, please use the [support site](https://support.bioconductor.org/).
:::

## Finding channels and following discussions

New members are subscribed to four channels to get started:

- `general`: Community discussions and updates.
- `random`: Informal chat.
- `introductions`: Introduce yourself and meet other members.
- `events`: Workshops, talks, and conferences.

There are also channels for scientific interests, software development, training, regional communities, and specific projects.

Click **Browse more channels** at the bottom of your channel list to explore and subscribe. You're welcome to join any public channel that interests you.

**You don't need to follow everything.** Start with a few channels, read along if you prefer, and join conversations when you have a question or something to share.

## A short tour and further help

Watch the [two-minute Zulip tour](https://static.zulipchat.com/static/navigation-tour-video/fffe1bb0baefab1a448fd9082738eaf271feb7ec247901242cd7bccb2280914b.mp4) for a demonstration of channels, topics, navigation, and starting a conversation.

For more detailed instructions, see Zulip's [getting-started guide](https://zulip.com/help/getting-started-with-zulip).

::: {.callout-note title="Our move from Slack"}
The community previously used [Slack](https://slack.com) for chat. We moved to Zulip on 2 June 2025 to ensure long-term access to discussions and better reflect the community's open-source values.

Read more in [Bioconductor is Moving from Slack to Zulip for Community Chat](https://blog.bioconductor.org/posts/2025-05-29-slack-to-zulip/).
:::
